headline: Your iRealty waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing Australian agency offices into the right iRealty offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Uthara (Thara) Nair, Head of Marketing.
productSummary: iRealty is smart email marketing built for Australian and New Zealand real estate, not borrowed from e-commerce. It syncs natively with Agentbox / Reapit, REX, Vault, and ReNet, then reads opens, suburb-report clicks, and listing engagement so agents know who in the CRM is warming up to sell. One-click newsletters (15 minutes, down from hours), automated follow-up, Bounce Protect, and a No Spam Guarantee. Homepage: 30% more appraisals, 35%+ open rates versus 19-22% industry, 3-5% of dormant contacts thinking about selling. Live in 10 days. 20+ years. Trusted by Ray White, LJ Hooker, McGrath, Belle Property, Raine & Horne, RE/MAX, Stockdale & Leggo, Elders, Century 21, First National, Highland, Harcourts, Place. 2026 REB Innovation Awards Finalist.
coreInsight: Thara already sells automated follow-up that turns a dormant CRM into listing conversations. The one TAM is AU/NZ agency offices realestate.com.au and Google Maps already list. The one routing signal is the live listing count on that same REA agency page, because one cheap AU-native scrape returns both the TAM and an integer that tells you whether they are drowning in volume follow-up, still building EDMs by hand, starving for listings from a cold database, or still in-TAM with no sale stock. Clay and Apollo AU contact search are not the spine. That is the coverage objection she already raised.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is the listing count REA already prints
sections.takeaway: realestate.com.au already names the agency office and already prints how many properties it has for sale. That integer is stronger than a Clay AU headcount guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every AU agency office
sections.takeaway: First match wins. High live listing counts go first, then mid-stock offices, then thin-stock offices, then every remaining in-TAM agency Maps or Domain still lists.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each listing band gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: High-stock offices get a seller-signal call list. Mid-stock offices get a 15-minute newsletter swap. Thin-stock offices get a dormant-database appraisal brief. The rest get the Database Growth Blueprint iRealty already publishes.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Who to call today, stop the EDM hours, win listings from the database you already own
sections.takeaway: The list is always AU/NZ agency offices, aimed at principals, agency owners, and marketing managers. Franchise brand and CRM name are merge tags, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the stock REA already shows
sections.takeaway: Notice the live listing count, poke the follow-up or dormant-database gap that count implies, then ask for a one-letter yes. No Clay-looking opener.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the high-stock offices first
sections.takeaway: Start where REA already shows a heavy live book. Prove reply density, then roll mid-stock, thin-stock, and the Database Growth Blueprint catch-all. Clay is never the list spine.

signalReasons: realestate.com.au agency pages are the TAM iRealty already sells into, Australian (and NZ) offices with a visible book of stock, and the live listing count in one pull.
The same scrape returns listing_count as an integer, which is enough to route high-stock, mid-stock, thin-stock, or remaining without a second enrichment product and without Clay AU coverage.

The ladder maps to live iRealty copy: seller-intent alerts so agents call first, one-click newsletters in 15 minutes, 3-5% of dormant contacts thinking about selling, and the Database Growth Blueprint for everyone else.
Franchise brand, suburb, CRM, and title are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last, never the TAM spine.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: High live stock
tiers.trigger: realestate.com.au (or Domain / NZ equivalent) shows listing_count >= 40 for the office. Cutoff estimated.
tiers.pain: The book is already heavy. Homepage: by the time a seller calls, they have already spoken to three other agents. Principals page: agents fall behind on follow-up when every send depends on manual effort. High live stock implies a large past-client database going cold while the team is busy on current deals.
tiers.valueProp: iRealty surfaces seller signals across the whole database so principals put agents on the right conversations first. Real-time engagement alerts. Homepage: 30% more appraisals. Principals page: >32% open rate across all accounts, real-time engagement signals. Reed & Co: 47 vendors shortlisted from a single campaign, 100% warm.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest intent. They already run a listings machine. Follow-up is the bottleneck iRealty is built for.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Mid live stock
tiers.trigger: listing_count 10-39, and not already Tier 1. Cutoff estimated.
tiers.pain: The office is active, but marketing is still hours of EDM. Principals page: newsletter creation down from hours to 15 minutes. Homepage: 1-click newsletters. Without a repeatable send, past clients go cold and the next appraisal is a guess.
tiers.valueProp: One-click, on-brand newsletters from listing and suburb data already in the CRM. Email page: 15 min newsletter build time. Customer-wins: O'Brien Real Estate, 3 offices live in 10 days, newsletter creation hours to 15 minutes. Bounce Protect and No Spam Guarantee keep sender reputation intact.
tiers.replyDensity: Strong. They already sell. The weekly EDM is still a grind.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Thin live stock
tiers.trigger: listing_count 1-9, and not already Tier 1 or 2. Cutoff estimated.
tiers.pain: The live book is thin. Homepage: the average Australian agency has 1,800+ dormant contacts, and statistically 3-5% of contacts not spoken to in six months are thinking about selling. Those listings are sitting in the CRM, not on REA.
tiers.valueProp: iRealty shows who is opening suburb reports and listing emails so agents call first. Homepage CTA: win more listings from the database you already own. Elders Newcastle: 60-70 leads in under 24 hours from a 9,000-contact database. Nathan Strudwick, Elders Shailer Park: best sales quarter in five months after starting iRealty.
tiers.replyDensity: Good. They need listings. The database they already own is the offer.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining TAM
tiers.trigger: Every remaining in-TAM AU/NZ agency office: zero current REA sale listings, Maps-only, Domain-only, rental-heavy, or listing_count not yet parsed
tiers.pain: They are still in the agency set iRealty sells into. The database is still the growth engine. Generic email tools still treat contacts like shoppers. About page: not a marketing platform that real estate was bolted onto.
tiers.valueProp: Built for real estate from day one. Native Agentbox / Reapit, REX, Vault, ReNet sync. Live in 10 days, done-for-you onboarding. Homepage magnet already on-site: The Database Growth Blueprint. Email page: trusted by 200+ agencies across Australia. 20+ years.
tiers.dataSource: REA / Domain / Maps TAM after higher tiers route out
tiers.replyDensity: Broadest coverage. Softest ask. Still 100% of TAM.

launchPlan: Pull realestate.com.au agency pages for Australia (and realestate.co.nz for New Zealand). Keep listing_count, named_suburb, office_name, franchise_group, and agency_website in the same export. Fill gaps from Domain.com.au and Google Maps Places in the Real estate agency category. This is the TAM spine. Do not start in Clay or Apollo.

Route on listing_count first-match: >= 40 Tier 1, >= 10 Tier 2, >= 1 Tier 3, remaining in-TAM catch-all. Those integer cutoffs are estimated and must be tuned after the first scrape, not treated as iRealty site numbers. Suppress already_customer at office level only. A Ray White or LJ Hooker logo on iRealty's homepage is not a franchise-wide exclude.

Resolve Principal, Licensee, Director, Agency Owner, and Head of Marketing from the agency team page, then LinkedIn Sales Navigator with an Australia / New Zealand geo filter. ASIC / ABR for officers when the site is thin. Title is a merge tag, not a second TAM.

Resolve work emails from the agency contact page first, then Hunter / Prospeo / Findymail. Apollo last, and only after the office is routed. Do not buy a raw Australian-real-estate Clay list. That is the coverage objection Thara already raised, and it is why REA + Maps is the spine.

Launch Tier 1 Seller-Signal Call List first. Smallest list, sharpest volume signal, closest to Addison's scrape-high-intent and principal-listings angles. Who-to-call-today copy as the control, 30% more appraisals as the A/B on the same list.

Add Tier 2 15-Minute Newsletter Swap once mid-stock merge tags are clean. Then Tier 3 Dormant Database Appraisal Brief. Turn on the Database Growth Blueprint catch-all last so every remaining in-TAM office still has a route.

Keep franchise_group, named_suburb, and crm_hint as merge tags, not campaign splits, until one listing-count tier is clearly working. Do not launch a tier under about 1,500 contacts; that threshold is the waterfall SOP, not an iRealty site number. Do not send Clay-looking openers. The notice line is always the live listing count REA already prints.

thresholds.action: Perfect. Scale that tier. Keep the winning call-timing, newsletter, appraisal, or blueprint variant.
Good. Let it run. Do not mix a non-agency TAM into this waterfall, and do not move the spine onto Clay AU coverage.
Borderline. Swap only the magnet or the first-line listing count. Do not change the route.

thresholds.rate: Worse than 1 per 500, or reply rate under 1% after 1,500+ sends
thresholds.action: Cut that copy variant. Keep the exclusive waterfall. Retune the estimated 40 / 10 listing cutoffs from the live scrape if a band is starved of contacts.
